subject: Archaeology
title: Side-Scan Sonar: Mapping the Invisible
description: Learn Side-Scan Sonar: Mapping the Invisible in one minute.

hook.text: Sonar can reveal a shipwreck hidden under sand and mud without anyone getting wet. Sound sees what eyes cannot.

buildup.text: Side-scan sonar tows a sensor behind a ship, sending sound waves sideways across the seabed and recording the echoes.

discovery.text: The resulting images show objects on the bottom in remarkable detail — cannons, anchors.

twist.text: Most 'wrecks' detected by sonar turn out to be rocks or modern debris. False positives waste months of dive time.

climax.text: Multibeam sonar now creates 3D seabed maps accurate to inches. Entire coastlines can be surveyed in days.

punchline.text: We can now map the ocean floor like a city street. Most of it is still unmapped.

quiz.question: What is a major challenge with side-scan sonar wreck detection?
options: Sound waves cannot penetrate deeper than 100 feet
Most detected objects turn out to be rocks or debris, not wrecks
Sonar only works in warm tropical waters
